title: Safety glasses pre-use inspection checklist (US, federal OSHA)
subtitle: Check eyewear against 29 CFR 1910.133 / 1926.102 and OSHA's nonmandatory Appendix B before each shift or task.
instructions: Check each pair before use and again whenever the task or hazard changes.
Take any pair that fails an item out of use and report it to whoever runs your hazard assessment.
Items marked Appendix B are OSHA guidance, not mandatory rule text.

sections.title: Marking and compliance
items: The frame or lens is distinctly marked so you can identify the manufacturer.
The manufacturer's documentation shows compliance with ANSI/ISEA Z87.1-2010, ANSI Z87.1-2003 or ANSI Z87.1-1989 (R-1998), or the employer has shown the device is at least as effective.
Lenses used against welding or cutting light are marked or identified as filter lenses, with a shade suited to the work. A tint alone doesn't count.

sections.title: Condition and fit
items: Built-in or detachable side shields are present and secure wherever flying objects are a hazard.
The eyewear fits snugly, is reasonably comfortable and doesn't unduly interfere with movement.
For dust or chemical splash tasks, the protector seals to the face all the way around.
Lenses are clean and not fogged. Clean them as often as conditions require.
The device can be cleaned and disinfected, especially if it is shared.
The eyewear is inspected, cleaned and maintained at regular intervals so it still gives the protection required.

sections.title: Wearer and combinations
items: Either protective eyewear with the prescription built in, or protection worn over glasses without pushing either set of lenses out of position.
They wear appropriate eye protection too. Watch for extra risk from dust or chemicals.
They are worn only over primary eye protection (spectacles or goggles).
Metal-frame eyewear is used with caution, or avoided, near electrical hazards.

references: 29 CFR 1910.133 Eye and face protection (general industry) and 29 CFR 1926.102 (construction), OSHA
29 CFR 1910 Subpart I Appendix B, nonmandatory hazard assessment and PPE selection guidance, OSHA
disclaimer: General guidance only, not legal advice. Check the current regulation and your employer's procedures.
